newsitem.title: CANADA: Govts, natives sign MOU on Voisey's Bay.
newsitem.headline: Govts, natives sign MOU on Voisey's Bay.

text.p: The governments of Canada and Newfoundland as well as officials representing native groups in Labrador said on Friday they have signed a memorandum of understanding for an environmental review of the mining plan at Voisey's Bay, Labrador.
The review will look at Inco Ltd's mine and mill plan to extract nickel, copper and cobalt from the huge Voisey's Bay metals deposits.
The memorandum of understanding will harmonize the environmental assessment processes of the two levels of government, the parties said in a release.
The memorandum was good news for Inco and its subsidiary, Voisey's Bay Nickel Co.
"What it means for us is the environmental process for the mine and the mill project can begin," Voisey's Bay Nickel spokesman Rick Gill said in a phone interview from St. John's, Newfoundland.
With the agreement signed, the probability of concluding the permit process by the end of May is good, Gill said.
Construction on the mine and the mill will proceed once the permits are granted, he explained.
"It means we're on track and making progress."
Gill said he expects the company will begin to produce concentrate from the mine before the end of 1999.

Native groups -- the Innu and the Inuit -- said last week their land claim negotiations with the federal and provincial governments had broken down. They hinted they would take steps to delay progress on the Voisey's Bay nickel deposit unless the governments were more flexible.
But the memorandum of understanding signed today showed the parties had cleared up the major roadblocks between them.

"This is a fair and balanced MOU," William Barbour, president of the Labrador Inuit Association, said in a statement. "It reflects the way that the Voisey's Bay project can respect the Inuit and be a win-win for everybody."
